Strait of Hormuz Status: October 3, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  217 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
3 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 National Herald, Gulf News and NDTV Profit report five Indian nationals were rescued after a projectile struck a Kuwait-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1.

02 Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven oil tankers were targeted in the Strait of Hormuz in five days.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a live combat zone for commercial shipping. On October 1, a projectile struck a Kuwait-flagged tanker in the strait; National Herald, Gulf News and NDTV Profit report that five Indian nationals were rescued in the aftermath. Oman's role in the rescue operation is noted by Gulf News, whose headline reads "Five Indians rescued with Oman's help after tanker struck in Strait of Hormuz." That October 1 attack follows a projectile strike on the Kuwaiti supertanker Al Funtas on September 28, reported in the prior cycle. Al Jazeera reports UK maritime authorities say two oil tankers were hit by unknown projectiles near the strait; the attacker has not been identified by any independent source. Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven oil tankers were targeted in the strait over a five-day span, a claim that should be treated as such given its source. The 43 indexed events in the last 24 hours reflect continued high operational tempo. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.25 as of 14:50 UTC, down 0.11% in the last session before the close; futures markets are shut, and that figure has not moved since close. As of 14:50 UTC, 158 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
